why: R11's `environment` signal asks whether our kernel declares anything about
a candidate held-out family's subject operators. It cannot be a threshold,
and measuring it is what shows why: `natural-square-root` is a legitimate
standing held-out family and we declare `Nat.sqrt`, `Nat.sqrt_zero` and
`Nat.sqrt_one` (draw 8 compared all four by hand; none is a mirror), while
a `natural-nth-root` candidate picks up 9 hits on the stem `root` whose top
is `Complex.root_of_unity_pow` -- unrelated mathematics sharing a word. No
count separates those. A person reading five names does, in a minute.
So a NEW held-out family whose sweep is non-empty must be reviewed here
before it may be drawn. The review must reproduce the LIVE sweep exactly:
that is what makes it a disclosure rather than a rubber stamp, because a
later declaration landing in that namespace changes the sweep and
invalidates the review instead of passing silently.
The DEMAND is scoped to draw time. Every standing held-out family was
preregistered before this screen existed, so demanding a review for one
retroactively would mean either a red gate on `main` or a file asserting
diligence nobody performed -- and the second is the checker-that-cannot-fail
defect wearing a paper trail. A STALE review is refused wherever it is
found, because that is a claim someone made.

natural-find-greatest.finding: Live sweep reproduced in this worktree against a FRESHLY REBUILT shape_search (env=2629, four declarations more than ADR-1160's 2625 -- Int.pow_neg_one_of_even/_odd, Int.secondSupplementaryLaw, Nat.half_ceil_parity, none of them touching this family). The four stems resolve to 24 declarations and every one was read by name against the ten drawn statements (Nat.findGreatest_eq, _eq_iff, _eq_zero_iff, _is_greatest, _le, _mono, _mono_left, _mono_right, _of_ne_zero, _of_not). NOTHING SETTLES ANY OF THEM, and two independent mechanical checks say so rather than a count: the environment dump contains the string `findGreatest` exactly ONCE and it is the Definition, and `shape_search --const Nat.findGreatest` is ABSENT -- run with a working positive control, which matters here because the FIRST control I used (`--concl Nat.countRange`) also returned ABSENT: `--concl` indexes the conclusion HEAD, which for an equation is `Eq`, so three earlier ABSENT verdicts of mine proved nothing. `--const Nat.countRange` is FOUND 21 and is the control the verdicts above are read against. `find_greatest.rs` carries one Declaration::Definition and zero `.theorem(` call sites, checked in the source rather than inherited from ADR-1160. STEM BY STEM. `decidable` (20) is the logic prelude's decidability plumbing -- Decidable, .and/.byCases/.decide/.decide_eq_true_iff/.em/.isFalse/.isTrue/.not/.ofBool/.of_decide_eq_false/.of_decide_eq_true/.or/.rec, DecidablePred -- plus Rat.decidable_le and three string-prelude equality deciders, all unrelated, and Nat.lnp_decidable, which is the one that needed real reading (below). `greatest` (2) is Int.gcd_greatest, the gcd characterization, an unrelated function sharing a word -- the same false-positive class natural-square-root's accepted review names -- and Nat.findGreatest itself. `decidablepred` (1) and `find` (1) are the two new constructions. THE AWKWARD FINDING, which the stem sweep reaches only by accident and which no gate flags: this kernel has a LEAST-number principle over decidable predicates, and one form of it is BOUNDED. Nat.lnp_bounded_search : forall (Q : Nat -> Prop), (forall n, Or (Q n) (Not (Q n))) -> forall n, Or (forall k, Lt k n -> Not (Q k)) (exists m, And (Lt m n) (And (Q m) (forall k, Lt k m -> Not (Q k)))) -- a bounded search over a pointwise-decided predicate WITH the extremality clause, which is the structural dual of what findGreatest_eq_iff and findGreatest_eq_zero_iff characterize. Its siblings are Nat.lnp_decidable (the Bool-valued form), Nat.lnp_of_pointwise_decision, Nat.lnp_unrestricted_implies_em and Nat.em_implies_lnp. NONE of them states any drawn row: they are about the LEAST element, they are free-standing existence disjunctions rather than characterizations of a defined function, and not one mentions Nat.findGreatest (which cannot occur in any of them -- it was declared yesterday and the --const query above is ABSENT). But a producer arriving at findGreatest_eq_zero_iff has lnp_bounded_search's induction-on-the-bound skeleton available and can transport it, so this family is materially less blind than a sweep of ['decidable', 'greatest', 'decidablepred', 'find'] suggests, and a held-out result here should be read knowing that. Recorded as a disclosure and not a refusal on ADR-0654's stated rule: a blind family must be allowed to use developed tools or nothing could ever be held out. FOUR MORE THINGS THE STEM SWEEP CANNOT REACH, enumerated by hand against the dump because a name-based screen is blind to a proof under a different name (the Mathlib.Data.Nat.Count failure this whole review exists because of). (1) Nat.exists_most_significant_bit : forall n, Not (Eq n zero) -> exists i, And (Eq (testBit n i) one) (forall j, Lt i j -> Eq (testBit n j) zero) is the nearest thing in the environment to findGreatest_is_greatest's CONTENT -- a greatest satisfying index, with everything above it failing. It is unbounded above, specific to testBit, and an existence statement rather than a function characterization, so it settles nothing here; its fuel-induction route (Nat.msb_exists_of_le_fuel) is another transportable skeleton and is disclosed for the same reason as the LNP family. (2) Nat.sqrt and Nat.nthRoot are bounded greatest-satisfying searches at specific predicates; Nat.sqrt carries only sqrt_zero/sqrt_one/no_rational_sqrt_two and Nat.nthRoot/nthRootAux carry no theorem at all, so none proves any of the ten. (3) Nat.nth/nthAux select the n-th ASCENDING witness, not the greatest below a bound, and likewise carry no theorem. (4) Nat.countRange and its 25 lemmas count witnesses; every one concludes about countRange and none about a greatest witness. Also read and cleared: Nat.least_divisor_search, Nat.leastResidue and Nat.least_residue_* (least-divisor / least-residue searches, unrelated predicates). REDUCTION CHECK, because ADR-1115's classifier is necessary and not sufficient. R12 reports 0 of 10 and that is true but weak: is_closed_evaluation is binder-free by construction, so a forall-quantified DEFINING EQUATION is invisible to it. Reading the ten instead: none is a boundary equation of Nat.findGreatest. The nearest is findGreatest_of_not : Not (P (n+1)) -> findGreatest P (n+1) = findGreatest P n, which is the else-branch of the recursion gated on a hypothesis -- NOT refl, because our construction branches through Decidable.byCases on `dp (succ m)`, a variable applied to a term, which never iota-reduces at a symbolic argument; the row needs the negative elimination supplied explicitly. The two rows that WOULD be refl, Nat.findGreatest_succ and Nat.findGreatest_zero, are pool rows 12 and 13 and fall outside the drawn ten by the alphabet alone (pool 15, drawn 0..9, re-measured here with select()'s own screen). No module was added or removed to put them there. A layout combining Mathlib.Data.Nat.Find with any other module changes which ten are drawn and must re-run this screen; draw 15 takes the module alone.

natural-integer-root.finding: Live sweep reproduced in this worktree against a FRESHLY REBUILT shape_search (declarations=2711), identical to ADR-1245's, and its redo of draw 11's natural-nth-root review is RE-DERIVED here rather than inherited. THE DRAWN TEN are Nat.ceilRoot_eq_zero, _ne_zero, _one_left, _one_right, _pow_self, _zero_left, _zero_right, Nat.dvd_ceilRoot_pow, Nat.dvd_pow_iff_ceilRoot_dvd and Nat.floorRoot_eq_zero. STEM BY STEM. `root` (13) resolves to three CReal.ivt_exact_root{,_at,_decides_sign} (bisection root-finding for the intermediate value theorem, a different carrier and a different question), six Complex.{I_is_fourth_root, IsRootOfUnity, geom_sum_eq_zero_of_root_of_unity, one_is_root_of_unity, root_of_unity_mul, root_of_unity_pow} (roots of unity), Nat.nthRoot/Nat.nthRootAux (draw 11's ORDER root) and Nat.ceilRoot/Nat.floorRoot (this family's own construction, necessarily self-matching). `ceil` (2) is Nat.ceilRoot and Nat.half_ceil_parity, the latter about the parity of (n+1)/2 and unrelated. `ceilroot` (1) is the definition. MECHANICAL, against a working positive control (--const Nat.countRange -> FOUND 21): --const Nat.ceilRoot, --const Nat.floorRoot and --const Nat.nthRoot are all ABSENT at declarations=2711 from a binary built in this worktree. No declaration in this kernel mentions any of the three in its type, so nothing has been proved about any of them. THE SWEEP DOES NOT REACH Nat.floorRoot, the same threshold gap as this draw's sibling review: Nat.floorRoot occurs in exactly ONE drawn row (Nat.floorRoot_eq_zero), below the max(2, 0.30 x 10) = 3 characteristic floor, so it is not a subject and the stems `floor` and `floorroot` are never swept even though a drawn row is about it. Swept by hand: `floorroot` -> 1 (the definition); `floor` -> 3 (Nat.floorRoot plus CReal.bucketIndexFloorLower and CReal.bucketIndexFloorUpper, the unit-fraction grid clamps in creal/uniform_continuity.rs). Empty -- but a review that ran only the automated sweep would not have known that. CARRIED FROM ADR-1245 AND RE-DERIVED: floorRoot/ceilRoot are DIVISIBILITY roots and Nat.nthRoot is an ORDER root. floorRoot 2 12 = 2, ceilRoot 2 12 = 6 and nthRoot 2 12 = 3, all three kernel-checked in nat_prelude/factorization_root_tests.rs rather than hand-computed. Substituting floorRoot into the held-out Nat.le_nthRoot_iff (a <= n.nthRoot b <-> a^n <= b) at (n,a,b) = (2,3,12) gives 3 <= 2 (false) <-> 9 <= 12 (true), so the two families' rows are not the same propositions. ALSO CARRIED: the stem sweep is a NAME sweep -- had ADR-1245 named these Nat.divisorFloor/Nat.divisorCeil the `root` sweep would not have moved at all while the adjacency question was exactly as live. THE NEW FINDING, and it is the awkward one. ADR-1245 framed the shape-2 risk PROSPECTIVELY -- whoever lands pow_dvd_iff_dvd_floorRoot and the rest of the supporting theorems from development must re-run this screen first -- and that is right and still stands. But the rhyme is ALREADY LIVE BETWEEN TWO BLIND ROWS, today, and nothing in this draw creates it: drawn Nat.ceilRoot_pow_self (n != 0 -> forall a, n.ceilRoot (a^n) = a) and standing held-out Nat.nthRoot_pow (n != 0 -> forall a, n.nthRoot (a^n) = a) are the SAME STATEMENT with a different root function; drawn Nat.ceilRoot_one_right against standing Nat.nthRoot_one_right; drawn Nat.ceilRoot_zero_left (= 0) against standing Nat.nthRoot_zero_left (= 1), same shape, different value; and drawn Nat.dvd_pow_iff_ceilRoot_dvd is the divisibility adjunction where standing Nat.le_nthRoot_iff is the order adjunction, which is exactly the rhyming pair ADR-1245 predicted. THIS IS NOT A LEAK AND R11 IS RIGHT TO BE CLEAN: ADR-0653's rule is about a held-out family whose mathematics a DEVELOPMENT or TRAIN family already publishes, natural-nth-root is held-out, nothing about Nat.nthRoot is published, and --const Nat.nthRoot is ABSENT. What it does mean is that the blind population's two `root` families are NOT INDEPENDENT SIGNALS: a route that establishes ceilRoot_pow_self very probably establishes nthRoot_pow by the same skeleton, so whoever reads a held-out result over either family should count the two as roughly one capability rather than two. Recorded because an undisclosed correlation inside a blind population overstates its breadth in exactly the way a leak does, by a different mechanism. VERDICT: our development settles nothing in the drawn ten, under any name. Draw.

natural-nth-root.finding: REDONE for ADR-1245 against env=2708, not amended: the previous review described env=2629 and its recorded sweep ([['root','CReal.ivt_exact_root',11],...]) no longer matched the live one, because Nat.ceilRoot and Nat.floorRoot (ADR-1245, this lane) took the stem 'root' from 11 declarations to 13. ALL 13 READ BY NAME: CReal.ivt_exact_root, CReal.ivt_exact_root_at, CReal.ivt_exact_root_decides_sign (bisection root-finding over CReal, an unrelated construction over a different carrier); Complex.I_is_fourth_root, Complex.IsRootOfUnity, Complex.geom_sum_eq_zero_of_root_of_unity, Complex.one_is_root_of_unity, Complex.root_of_unity_mul, Complex.root_of_unity_pow (roots of unity over Complex, unrelated mathematics sharing the word 'root'); Nat.nthRoot, Nat.nthRootAux (this draw's own ADR-0910 construction, necessarily self-matching); and the two NEW ones, Nat.ceilRoot and Nat.floorRoot. The 'nth' stem's four are Nat.nth and Nat.nthAux (draw 7's natural-nth-selector well-founded selector, a different function despite the shared stem) plus nthRoot/nthRootAux again; the 'nthroot' stem's two are nthRoot/nthRootAux. THE ONLY NEW QUESTION IS WHETHER THE TWO NEW DECLARATIONS SETTLE ANY DRAWN ROW, AND THEY DO NOT -- they are different functions, measured rather than argued. Nat.nthRoot n a is the greatest m with m^n <= a (an ORDER statement); Nat.floorRoot n a is the greatest b with b^n | a and Nat.ceilRoot n a the least b >= 1 with a | b^n (DIVISIBILITY statements, the adjoints of b |-> b^n on the divisor lattice). They disagree at small arguments and the committed test suite pins the disagreement: factorization_root_tests::the_two_roots_disagree_with_each_other_and_with_the_numeric_root asserts floorRoot 2 12 = 2, ceilRoot 2 12 = 6 AND nthRoot 2 12 = 3, the last so the disagreement cannot be vacuous through a broken nthRoot. The boundary conventions differ too: nthRoot 0 a = 1 while ceilRoot 0 a = floorRoot 0 a = 0. Substituting floorRoot into a drawn row makes it FALSE, not merely unproved: Nat.le_nthRoot_iff reads a <= n.nthRoot b <-> a^n <= b, and at (n,a,b) = (2,3,12) the floorRoot form is 3 <= 2 (false) <-> 9 <= 12 (true). MECHANICAL CHECKS, each with a working positive control (shape_search --include-constructed --const Nat.countRange is FOUND 21 at declarations=2708): --const Nat.nthRoot is ABSENT, so no declaration in this kernel mentions Nat.nthRoot anywhere in its type and the kernel has still never proved a theorem ABOUT it -- the same finding as the previous review, re-derived at the new environment rather than inherited. --const Nat.ceilRoot and --const Nat.floorRoot are ABSENT as well, which is ADR-0653's construction-only promise measured rather than asserted. The ten drawn rows are UNCHANGED by these declarations: ADR-1245's screen ran the frozen-family drawn-ten churn check and 0 of 42 families churn, so no row was added, removed or reordered. R11's topic, vocabulary and environment-threshold signals are all clean; the stale review was the single refusal reason and this row is what clears it. TWO THINGS RECORDED BECAUSE THEY ARE AWKWARD, NEITHER OF WHICH REFUSES THE FAMILY. (1) The stem sweep is a NAME sweep: ceilRoot/floorRoot matched it only because they contain the letters 'root', and it could not have told a divisibility root from an order root either way -- had this lane named them Nat.divisorFloor the sweep would not have moved at all, and the genuine adjacency question would have been exactly as live. The count is a trigger for reading, never evidence on its own. (2) A SHAPE adjacency does exist and should be watched: Nat.pow_dvd_iff_dvd_floorRoot (a^n | b <-> a | n.floorRoot b) is the divisibility adjunction, and the held-out Nat.le_nthRoot_iff (a <= n.nthRoot b <-> a^n <= b) is the order adjunction, so their PROOF SKELETONS would rhyme. Nothing of the sort exists today (both --const probes ABSENT), and R11 asks whether a drawn row is settled, which it is not. But the lane that lands factorization_root's supporting theorems from development should re-run this screen first: that is the documented shape-2 blindness, and it would arrive through a legitimate development proof rather than through anything a name comparison sees.

natural-primitive-recursion.finding: Live sweep reproduced in this worktree against a FRESHLY REBUILT shape_search (declarations=2711, three more than ADR-1245's 2708 -- Int.firstSupplementaryLawResidue, Int.wilsonHalfSplit, Nat.sub_sub_self, none of them touching this family; gen-autogenesis-nursery-refill.py --check regenerates the manifest byte-identically under the refreshed snapshot, checked rather than assumed because ADR-1095's refresh displaced two train rows). THE DRAWN TEN are Nat.Primrec.add, .casesOn', .casesOn1, .const, .mul, .of_eq, .pow, .prec1, .pred and .swap. STEM BY STEM. `primrec` (9) is exactly ADR-1240's construction and nothing else: the inductive Nat.Primrec, its seven constructors (zero, succ, left, right, pair, comp, prec) and the recursor Nat.Primrec.rec -- necessarily self-matching, and DISJOINT from the drawn ten by name and by statement. The near miss is real and is not one: Nat.Primrec.prec is the general two-premise constructor and the drawn Nat.Primrec.prec1 is its specialization at a constant m, a different proposition that needs a derivation. `pair` (20) is dominated by word collisions across four carriers -- Nat.Pair and its eight projections/extensionality lemmas are the PAIR INDUCTIVE from the binaryRec lane, a structure type rather than Cantor pairing; Nat.restrict_pair_injective, Nat.restrict_pair_maps_into and Int.prod_range_pairing_collapse are the Wilson/totient transposition-pairing lemmas, stated over injectiveOn/mapsInto and mentioning Nat.pair nowhere (verified by their rendered types, not by their names); CPoint.cevian_pair_meet, CReal.geom_pair_within and Rat.PairwiseUncorrelated share only the word. The genuinely Nat.pair-related hits are Nat.pair, Nat.unpairLeft, Nat.unpairRight and Nat.unpaired (ADR-1220's constructions) plus Nat.Primrec.pair. `unpaired` (1) is the definition. MECHANICAL, each run against a working positive control (shape_search --const Nat.countRange -> FOUND 21): --const Nat.Primrec -> FOUND 8, the seven constructors and the recursor; --const Nat.pair -> FOUND 3 (Nat.Primrec.pair, .prec, .rec); --const Nat.unpaired -> FOUND 2 (Nat.Primrec.prec, .rec). NO THEOREM in this kernel mentions Nat.Primrec, Nat.pair or Nat.unpaired in its type at all. THE SWEEP DOES NOT REACH Nat.casesOn, and that is a gap in the SCREEN rather than in the family. subject_constants keeps a constant characteristic of at least max(2, 0.30 x 10) = 3 rows; Nat.casesOn occurs in exactly two drawn rows (casesOn', casesOn1), so it is not a subject and the stem `caseson` is never swept even though two drawn rows are about it. Swept by hand: EXACTLY ONE declaration, Nat.casesOn itself, ADR-1240's definition, with nothing stated about it. THE STEM SWEEP IS A NAME SWEEP (ADR-1245's finding, and it applies here verbatim): had ADR-1240 named the predicate Nat.PrimitiveRecursive the `primrec` stem would not have moved at all while the adjacency question was exactly as live, and had it named it Nat.Rec the sweep would have been swamped by unrelated recursors. The count is a trigger for reading; it is never evidence on its own, and the reading is what answers this. REVIEWED FOR DRAW 17 AND REFUSED, so this is a `refused` row and not a `reviews` licence -- this file's own how_to_add_a_row says "if you found a mirror, do not write a row", and this review found four. R11's three HARD signals are CLEAN and that is not the problem: topic 0, vocabulary 0 of 10, R9 0 of 10, R12 clean, pool 22 against a floor of 10. WHAT REFUSES IT IS THE ENVIRONMENT SWEEP THIS DISCLOSURE EXISTS TO FORCE. `Nat.count dec n := Nat.countRange dec n` (nat_prelude/count_and_div_max_pow.rs, ADR-1430) is a DEFINITIONAL ALIAS, and the kernel carries 22 `countRange` lemmas -- re-counted from kernel-environment-snapshot-v1.json's declaration list, not from the module doc, which says 19. Row by row against the drawn ten, with kernel types read from `nat_theorem_inventory` rather than from names: (1) Nat.count_add, `count p (a+b) = count p a + count (fun k => p (a+k)) b`, IS `Nat.countRange_split` term for term, including the shifted predicate. (2) Nat.count_le, `count p n <= n`, IS `Nat.countRange_le`. (3) Nat.count_mono_left, `(forall k<n, p k -> q k) -> count p n <= count q n`, IS `Nat.countRange_le_of_subset`, whose hypothesis `Nat.Subset p q n` is DEFINED in finite_set.rs as `forall k, k < n -> p k = true -> q k = true` -- the same hypothesis verbatim. (4) Nat.count_monotone, `Monotone (count p)`, IS `Nat.countRange_le_of_le` unbundled. (5) Nat.count_lt_count_succ_iff is ENTAILED by the strictly stronger declared equation `Nat.countRange_succ` (`countRange p (succ n) = countRange p n + (if p n then 1 else 0)`), which decides the `<` in both directions by one Bool.rec on `p n`. Three more are half-declared: count_iff_forall's easy direction is countRange_congr_lt composed with countRange_const_true, and count_ne_iff_exists / count_iff_forall_not are the counting-witness argument countRange_succ_of_true and countRange_ge_two_of_two_witnesses already run. Only Nat.count_injective is genuinely untouched; count_add' is countRange_split's mirror. R9 REPORTS 0 OF 10 AND THAT IS R9 WORKING AS DESIGNED: it compares the drawn MATHLIB NAME against the environment, and the names differ (`count` vs `countRange`). R11's vocabulary screen reports 0 of 10 for the same reason one remove out -- `Nat.countRange` is kernel development, not the subject constant of any nursery development/train FAMILY, so nothing in the vocabulary map can reach it. The stem sweep (`count`, 46) is the ONLY signal in the entire guard that sees this, which is exactly the case ADR-0768 built the disclosure for. SECOND AND INDEPENDENT REASON, AND IT IS WORSE: Mathlib's `Nat.count : (Nat -> Prop) -> [DecidablePred p] -> Nat -> Nat` against ours `(Nat -> Bool) -> Nat -> Nat`. That is the SAME type divergence mirror-divergence-registry.json records for `Nat.nth` ("Bool vs Prop domain ... the mirror is a different proposition per the mirror-flip criterion's own 'different types' clause") and a LARGER one than `Nat.findGreatest`'s, which is registered on explicit-versus-instance-implicit DecidablePred alone. By the registry's own standard applied consistently, every Mathlib.Data.Nat.Count mirror is unclosable here -- and unclosable rows in held-out are the dead weight ADR-1445 measured at 31 rows across four families, not blind population. Either reason disqualifies the family alone; they are different reasons and do not cancel. TWO CORRECTIONS TO count_and_div_max_pow.rs's module doc, both measured: it says the kernel has "no List and no DecidablePred" -- `List` is genuinely absent from the environment snapshot, but `DecidablePred.{u}` IS declared (prelude.rs:356) and is in the snapshot as a real declaration, not a bridge alias; and it says 19 countRange lemmas where the snapshot has 22. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS FAMILY DRAWABLE: nothing about the family. It is drawable as `development` or `train` the moment some held-out-safe family's primary module sorts lexicographically before Mathlib.Data.Nat.Count -- measured exhaustively for draw 17, 902 subsets of the 10 such unowned modules reach the ten-row floor and ZERO are viable, so that needs a construction lane (ADR-1420 Route 1).
